newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 19.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 19.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK FTSE index finished lower for the third consecutive day after a roller-coaster ride prompted by economic data here and in the U.S. which kept fears of higher interest rates alive. The FTSE 100 index finished just off the day's worst levels down 24.6 points at 4,332.2.

FRANKFURT - The Germany's DAX index ended bourse trade higher after late rally, boosted by a strong performance by individual shares in the chemical, banking and utility sectors, overall, shares still lack inspiration to forge new significant gains, but ended well above psychologically-key 3,300-point level. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,315.93 up 24.74 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,305.72.

PARIS - French stocks rebounded from two days of falls, helped by rising U.S. shares, slightly bigger than expected rise in the U.S. consumer price index, which rose 0.3 percent in February, stoked simmering expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates but the U.S. stockmarket pushed higher in early trading. The CAC-40 index closed up 22.82 points or 0.89 percent to 2,596.77.

ZURICH - The Swiss share market ended two days of decline, closing higher after fluctuating during much of the session, but dealers said there was no clear direction to trading and nervousness remained high. The All-share Swiss Performance Index was up 8.04 points or 0.28 percent to 2,879.50.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended slightly higher, continuing to benefit from government plans to breathe life into the property market, selling to make up for shortfalls ahead of the end-March book closing also added to the downward pressure. The Nikkei average finished at 18,493.71 up 48.51 points or 0.26 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower, after falling steadily in late afternoon, chiefly on selling in HSBC Holdings and a lack of buying interest before a U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting. The Hang Seng Index closed 97.49 points lower at 12,651.42.

SYDNEY - A late buying spree pushed Australian shares off their lows to finish just under 20 points down most of the weakness coming from futures selling and a softer Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index ended 19.10 points lower at 2,385.20.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended strong after trading in a narrow range in the morning, pushed up by futures activity, Gold shares retreated somewhat in the afternoon session after rising in early trade. The Overall index ended up 14.0 points to 7,099.5, the Industrial index gained 21.0 to 8,342.6 and the Gold index added 5.1 to 1,375.6.
